episodes.172611: A deep fetch of subtropical moisture streaming over New Mexico allowed scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms with heavy rainfall to impact parts of the region. A couple thunderstorms along the Continental Divide became strong with gusty outflow winds, frequent lightning strikes, and hail. One of the stronger storms produced a brief landspout tornado near Lake Valley, NM in San Juan County. No damage or injuries occurred with this brief storm.
episodes.173018: A strong cold front moved into the Central New York during the early morning hours on the 22nd. Thunderstorms developed along and ahead of the cold front. There was enough instability to support a severe thunderstorm that had strong wind gusts.
episodes.173121: A line of heavier showers moved across southwest Colorado early in the morning in response to a midlevel circulation overhead. Some localized street flooding occurred across portions of La Plata County as a result.
episodes.173131: A cold front moved through southern New England during the late morning and early afternoon triggering scattered thunderstorms.
episodes.173190: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.173191: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.173246: A mid to upper-level low pressure system moved southward and parked itself off the north-central California coast. Widespread rainfall occurred on the 18th, with some embedded heavier rain. The next couple of days showers and isolated thunderstorms |observed with locally very heavy rain. One such shower brought just over 2.5 inches of rain in 45 minutes near the town of Willits and caused some flooding on the Willits Bypass. Several SPSs and FLAs were issued during the span of a couple days for stronger thunderstorms and the accompanying heavy rain.
episodes.173370: Southwest flow during the late morning and early afternoon hours of September 21st advected warm, high dewpoint air into the region that was unusual for late September.  By late afternoon, a pre-frontal trough entered the area.   Thunderstorms crossing Lake Erie and arriving in western Pennsylvania during the late afternoon were hindered by warm air aloft, and thus were not able to achieve the overall coverage and intensity that had been anticipated.  Nevertheless, renewed convection along a cold front provided sufficient lift to create more widespread storms after midnight on the 22nd, and a few instances of wind damage resulted.
episodes.173371: Southwest flow during the late morning and early afternoon hours of September 21st advected warm, high dewpoint air into the region that was unusual for late September.  Late afternoon thunderstorms generally stayed closer to Lake Erie, but a cluster of storms managed to form in central Ohio after sunset, working their way east thereafter. These storms had strong enough wind gusts to create a few instances of damage.

episodes.174051: A northward surge in tropical moisture will resulted widespread showers and thunderstorms across northern Arizona.  Heavy rain over far northcentral Arizona and south central Utah resulted in a flash flood. A strong rotating thunderstorms also developed over far eastern Arizona.
episodes.174052: Deep moisture over northern Arizona, cooling aloft, and forcing from a low pressure lifting into Montana and Wyoming lead to scattered to widespread showers and thunderstorms over northern Arizona.
episodes.174139: A deep upper level low coming ashore along the U.S. West Coast resulted in a combination of strong forcing, instability, and available moisture over the Salt Lake City forecast area. This event prompted an uncommon issuance of a Severe Thunderstorm Watch (number 541 of the year). Scattered strong wind gusts occurred, as did multiple instances of Flash Flooding.
episodes.174185: Several occurrences of severe thunderstorm wind gusts and flooding with heavy rain were reported on September 21st.
episodes.174206: High pressure across the southern Plains and low pressure across the Great Basin led to a southerly flow across the region, advecting deep moisture. PWATs rose to 2, which was near record for the period, and with the increased moisture instability values also rose with MLCAPE values in excess of 2,000 J/KG. The forcing from the aforementioned low pressure helped to enhance the thunderstorm activity as it was moving from south to north.
episodes.174220: A thunderstorm moved south of Powder River Pass and produced a downburst that uprooted or snapped several trees near the Doyle Creek Campground. Damage to the campground was limited to trees and no injuries were reported.
episodes.174355: Two rounds of severe thunderstorms developed ahead of, and along, a cold front as it moved over the waters. These storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.174480: Cold and unstable air flowed southward into the region with the first push of Canadian air of the season into western New York. This resulted in a broad pool of mid-level cold air pushing over the relatively warm waters of the Great Lakes. Due to the shear profile, thunderstorms developed over the Great Lakes and resulted in isolated waterspouts. Further, during and subsequent to peak daytime heating, there was enough instability and shear to result in a few damaging wind gusts.

episodes.174604: On the morning of September 22nd a rare early morning severe thunderstorm dropped quarter to half dollar size hail to parts of Rockingham County.  A cold front was passing through New England during the morning, with a line of heavy rain showers and thunderstorms pushing across Southern New England.  The northern extension of this line of storms moved across Southern New Hampshire, where a cluster of storms interacted with the sea breeze front.  This enhanced the storms to become severe with damaging hail occurring over a half hour period.  In addition, isolated wind damage was also reported further inland along the New Hampshire and Massachusetts border region.

events.narrative: CoCoRaHS report of 2.58 inches of rain in 45 minutes. 1 to 2 inches of water was observed on the Willits Bypass which stopped traffic. Water quickly subsided after the thunderstorm.
Several trees were downed between Union, Walton and Verona.
A couple of trees were downed in the Granville area.
The Raft River RAWS measured a 73 mph wind gust.

The Groome weather station recorded an initial peak gust of 66 mph at 5:39 pm MST, with final lesser gusts of 63 mph at 6:05 and 6:06 pm MST. These wind gusts were  associated with a cluster of strong thunderstorms and their associated outflow winds which were moving through the area.
A tree was reported to be blown down on Route 666 just south of Dresden.

Video showed Arizona Department of Public Safety performed a swift water rescue by air around 2100MST. A family of 6 (2 parents and 4 kids) in an SUV were washed off of Val Vista Road near Warren Road at a low water crossing with Vekol Wash. Floodwaters were over the hood of the SUV after being pushed downstream. All 6 individuals were safely rescued from the roof of their vehicle and were unharmed. A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge on Vekol Wash near I-8, located approximately 14 miles southwest, showed the flow going above alarm stage at 1340 MST, peaking at 7.80 feet (2465 cfs) at 1540 MST, and returning below alarm stage at 1754 MST. A news article mentioned this was the second swift water rescue performed in a matter of a few hours. Details on the other rescue were not found.
A tree was reported to be blown down at the intersection of Main Street and Muskingum Avenue.

Ralston Road at the Vekol Wash low water crossing in Ak-Chin Village was flooded and was impassable for several hours. Peak floodwater height was measured at nearly 7 feet at around 1951 MST by the Pinal County Flood Control gauge at the crossing. Timing estimated based off when the water level first reached 1 feet deep. No damages or injuries were reported.

Heavy rain from nearby thunderstorms resulted in 3-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor estimates of around 1 to 2 inches total. Garfield County Dispatch reported flooding in Tropic, Cannonville, and Henrieville. One basement was flooded. Time estimated by radar.
Several large trees damaged with a few down along East Fork or Rock Creek east, southeast of Rockland.
A funnel cloud reported south of Pocatello near the Portneuf gap.
Heavy rain over far south-central Utah and far north-central Arizona resulted in a flash flood through Paria Canyon. The river gauge near the Colorado River showed almost a 4 foot rise.

Extensive street and road flooding occurred on the evening of the 21st in the Pocatello/Chubbuck area as rains in excess of a half inch fell.  The intersection of East Oak St and Yellowstone Ave flooded.  The Center Street Underpass accumulated 18 to 24 inches of water.  Flooding at N 3rd Ave and E Fremont St affected a business.  Hawthorne Rd flooded with deep water at the interstate 86 underpass and was closed from 830 pm to 10 pm MDT.  US Route 30 also closed between Hawthorne Rd and W Cedar St.
Power lines and a large limb were reported to be blown down.

Nearby thunderstorms with moderate rainfall resulted in 3-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor accumulation estimates of around 0.25 to 0.75 inches. The Pine Creek near Escalante stream gauge spiked to a peak flow of 228 CFS at 7:15 pm MST.
A tree was blown down by thunderstorm win on to State Route 209.
A tree was reported to be blown down by thunderstorm wind at the intersection of Walnut Grove Road and Stone Church Road.
A tree was downed across Grimes Road.
The English Village weather station recorded a peak wind gust of 62 mph as a result of a thunderstorm and associated outflow winds moving over the site.

The Logan Peak weather station recorded an initial peak wind gust of 63 mph at 9:00 pm MST as a result of a thunderstorm and associated outflow winds moving over the site. A second thunderstorm an hour later resulted in a wind gust of 58 mph at 10:00 pm MST.
The SR-201 at I-80, weather station recorded a wind gust of 65 mph as a result of a thunderstorm and associated outflow winds moving over the site.

A thunderstorm moved through portions of the Escalante River drainage basin, producing moderate rainfall, with widespread 3-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates of 0.50 to 1.00 inches in upstream tributary areas. This generated a flood wave that propagated downstream, resulting in the Escalante near Escalante river gauge spiking to  804 CFS at 9:50 pm MST.
The Gas Caves RAWS recorded a 58 mph wind gust.
Trees were reported downed onto a road.
The Beach weather station recorded a wind gust of 77 mph as a result of a thunderstorm and associated outflow winds moving over the site.
The I-80 at MP 107 weather station recorded a wind gust of 58 mph as a result of a thunderstorm and associated outflow winds moving over the site.
The Cardiff Peak weather station recorded a peak wind gust of 64 mph as a result of outflow winds from a nearby thunderstorm moving over the site.
Multiple trees were reported downed onto Route 19.
Trees were reported down.
Trees were reported downed onto power lines.
Trees were reported down near Hillsville Road.
Trees were blown down along US Route 62.
Trees were reported down.
Near Kelly Road, trees were blown down.
Strong thunderstorm winds knocked down power lines, resulting in a power outage on Seneca Blvd.
Convective outflow wind gusts associated with a severe thunderstorm downed trees along State Route 119 in Rindge, New Hampshire.
A severe thunderstorm dropped half dollar size hail in southeast of Kingston.
A severe thunderstorm dropped half dollar size hail in Exeter, New Hampshire.
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter size hail in Stratham, New Hampshire.
In Charlton, a lightning strike caused a house fire on H Foote Rd.
Minor street flooding occurred at the intersection of Main Ave and 32nd Street in Durango as a result of heavy rain from showers. A few rocks were in the road.
